newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Jan 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES - The second airport saga was diverted to Bang Pu yesterday just two days after the cabinet informally suspended the Nong Ngu Hao project in favour of an expanded Don Muang.

Parinya Narkchattree, deputy permanent secretary for interior, said PM Chavalit Yongchaiyudh proposed a business and convention center be built on 50,000-300,000 rai (8,103-48,622 hectares) reclaimed from the sea. (BANGKOK POST) - The United States will seek an explanation from the Thai government on its decision Tuesday to suspend work on the new international airport at Nong Ngu Hao, a move affecting US companies involved in the mammoth project. (THE NATION)

- The Assembly of the Poor will step up its pressure campaign on the Chavalit Yongchaiyudh government to implement measures contained in a Cabinet resolution to address problems faced by disadvantaged people. The measures were passed after protests by the group nearly nine months ago.
The group plans to stage rallies outside Government House beginning on Saturday following a meeting between representatives of the group and the govenment officials. (THE NATION) + + + +

- Italian Thai Development Plc is confident it will be able to hang on to a land deal with the Philippines government despite strong resistance from some quarters within that government. (BANGKOK POST)
- Thailand plans to ask Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum members to liberalise processed agriculture products at the annual APEC ministerial meeting in Canada later this year. (THE NATION)

- The continued appreciation of the U.S. dollar against the Japanese yen convinced several bankers that the dollar might reach 140 level and then it will be time for Thailand to review its basket of currency.

The bankers forecast that the dollar/yen exchange rate might soon pass the 130 level and reach 140 yen later. Such an appreciation would drive the dollar/baht exchange rate to a level which could severely harm Thailand's economy. (THE NATION)
